title: The Label Printer
briefing: Every part that leaves ByteWorks needs a neat label. The scanner is ancient, though: it reads part codes with extra spaces and in lowercase, like '  ram-0042  '. Clean up the code and print a proper label like RAM #0042 before we open the first production floor.
hints: String methods are used with a dot: raw_code.strip() removes the spaces and .upper() makes it capitals. You can chain them: raw_code.strip().upper().
Slicing: clean[:3] gives the first 3 characters and clean[-4:] gives the last 4. An f-string drops variables into text: f"{part_type} #{number}".
clean = raw_code.strip().upper(), part_type = clean[:3], number = clean[-4:], label = f"{part_type} #{number}", sku = clean.replace("-", ""), is_ram = clean.startswith("RAM"), then print(label)
bonus: Use .split('-') on clean to break it into a list of pieces. What do you get? (You'll learn about lists tomorrow!)
